chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: Johnny Hodges on Charlie Parker
summary: Hodges first said Parker had no sound, then later praised him after the 'Funky Blues' record for Granz.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: A funny thing, too, I was just reminded of it... I asked Johnny Hodges, when Bird first come on the scene... I said to him, "What do you think of Charlie Parker?" He said, "Ah, he don't play nothin'. He don't play nothin'." I said, "No?" He said, "He ain't got no sound." I said, "Charlie Parker ain't got no sound?" So I said, "Okay." So I got a chance... When I worked with Duke, I asked Johnny... It's the first thing I did. I said, "What do you think...?"
How many years later was that?

This was way later. I said, "What do you think of Charlie Parker?" He said, "Oh, he was beautiful." I said, "But Johnny, you told me he didn't have no sound." He said, "Well, I didn't know what I was talking about. He's one of the baddest..." But I mean, that was after they had made that Blues thing...
Yeah. Ha-ha, Bird let everybody know where
he was at. But anyway, I just brought that up because I think that people should know about such things.

Yeah. Just a funky blues, and Bird played the shit out of it! Johnny Hodges, I felt sorry for him, because if I was him, I wouldn't have played! "Let him finish making this record; I don't want to make this one." But boy, it was somethin' else.
